'''Lawrence M. Rudner''' is a research statistician and consultant whose work spans domains, including, statistical analysis, [[computer programming]], [[web development]], and [[oyster farming]]. He is the owner and president of Oyster Girl Oysters,<ref name=ala>{{cite web|url=https://oystergirl.us/who.htm|title= Oyster Girl Oysters Staff - Lawrence M. Rudner (Larry)}}</ref> and is an instructor at the Chesapeake Forum<ref name=qpq>{{cite web|url=https://chesapeakeforum.org/instructor/larry-rudner-ph-d/|title=Larry Rudner, Ph.D.}}</ref> and the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum. He is the founder and former editor of the ''Practical Assessment, Research, and Evaluation'' journal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholarworks.umass.edu/pare/editorialboard.html|title=Practical Assessment, Research, and Evaluation}}</ref>

Rudner has conducted research on measurement topics, including using Item Response Theory, IRT, for assessing item bias, parameter invariance, [[Person-fit analysis|person fit validity]], and classification accuracy, utilizing research methods, [[psychometrics]], [[data analysis]], and [[programming language]]s.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iacat.org/conference/keynote-addresses/|title=2019 IACAT Conference Registration}}</ref> He has written more than 150 scholarly papers and 40 grants, with contributions featured in books and chapters published by institutions,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://talbotspy.org/ai-101-a-brief-look-at-artificial-intelligence-with-lawrence-rudner-ph-d/|title=AI 101: A Brief Look at Artificial Intelligence with Lawrence Rudner, Ph.D.}}</ref> earning him the Award for Outstanding Dissemination of Educational Measurement Concepts to the Public from [[National Council on Measurement in Education]],<ref name=aqq>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncme.org/about/awards/ncme-awards/annual-award|title=Annual Award for Exceptional Achievement in Educational Measurement}}</ref> and the Career Achievement Award from the Association of Test Publishers.<ref name=zll>{{cite web|url=https://www.testpublishers.org/wall-of-honor|title=THE CAREER ACHIEVEMENT AWARD}}</ref>

Rudner held the position of senior fellow at the [[American Institutes for Research]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/009102609202100202|title=Pre-Employment Testing and Employee Productivity}}</ref>

==Education==
Rudner earned his Bachelor of Science in mathematics from [[Syracuse University]] in 1971. He continued his education with a Master of Science in [[Education]] from [[Western Connecticut State University]] in 1972 and completed his Doctorate in [[Psychology]] and [[Evaluation]] at [[Catholic University of America|The Catholic University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dlib.org/dlib/april03/authors/04authors.html|title=Authors in the April 2003 Issue of D-Lib Magazine}}</ref> In 1991, he pursued an MBA in [[Finance]] and [[Entrepreneurship]] at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED338157.pdf|title=Agency Theory, Incentives, and Student Loans}}</ref>

==Career==
Rudner served as the head of the Educational Resources Information Center (ERIC) Clearing House on Assessment,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.edweek.org/education/research-unexplored-territory/1999/12|title=Research: Unexplored Territory}}</ref> and as project officer for the [[National Assessment of Educational Progress]]. From 2004 to 2014, he was the vice president for Research and Psychometrics at the [[Graduate Management Admission Council|Graduate Management Admission Council (GMAC)]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gmac.com/-/media/files/gmac/research/employment-outlook/2014-corporaterecruiters-final-release-3.pdf|title=Corporate Recruiters Survey}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED540682.pdf|title=Demystifying the GMAT: Computer-Based Testing Terms}}</ref>

Prior to joining GMAC, Rudner was a senior associate (GS-15) in the US Government, where he was the project officer for the National Assessment of Educational Progress (NAEP), director of the [[Education Resources Information Center|ERIC]] Clearinghouse on Assessment and Evaluation,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/ED403282.pdf|title=The ERIC Clearinghouse on Assessment and Evaluation, 1995 Annual Report}}</ref> and a faculty member at universities.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://talbotspy.org/under-attack-the-history-of-cyberwarfare-yesterday-and-today/|title=Under Attack: The History of Cyberwarfare: Yesterday and Today}}</ref> Since 2021, he has been an instructor at the Chesapeake Forum, teaching courses on [[artificial intelligence]], [[Cyber-security regulation|cybersecurity]], and [[internet safety]] and the Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum, teaching classes on oyster gardening.<ref name=qpq/>

Rudner has been serving as the owner and president of Oyster Girl Oysters. Along with Willem Roosenburg, he invented a cost-effective oyster cage flipping system for which he received a patent in 2024. He has also authored a paper on predicting oyster volume for the East Coast Shellfish Growers Association.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ecsga.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/RudnerOysterModel.pdf|title=Developing an efficient oyster sorting schedule}}</ref>

==Contributions to the field==
Rudner created some of the first tools for first engines for [[automated essay scoring]], automated test assembly, and [[Computerized adaptive testing|computer adaptive testing]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.learntechlib.org/p/95815/|title=An Overview of Three Approaches to Scoring Written Essays by Computer}}</ref> He devised an AI method for documenting [[copyright infringement]]s receiving a US patent in 2009<ref>{{cite web|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/US7542989B2/en|title=Method and system for searching, identifying, and documenting infringements on copyrighted information}}</ref> and developed the Bayesian Essay Test Scoring System, a Windows-based [[Open-source software|open-source program]] for automated essay scoring applicable to various text classification tasks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edres.org/betsy/|title=Bayesian Essay Test Scoring sYstem - BETSY}}</ref><ref name=ssp>{{cite web|url=https://ejournals.bc.edu/index.php/jtla/article/view/1668|title=Automated Essay Scoring Using Bayes' Theorem}}</ref> He created an online interactive tutorial on [[decision theory]] comparing it with [[Item Response Theory]] and exploring the calibration sample size needed for accurate classifications.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://edres.org/mdt/home3.asp|title=An Evaluation of Measurement Decision Theory}}</ref>

Rudner directed the activities of the ERIC Clearinghouse on Assessment and Evaluation.<ref name=ssp/> One of his key projects was developing the Search ERIC Wizard, a search engine for the ERIC database that used a [[thesaurus]] as a front end.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://digitalcommons.usf.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1351&context=usf_EPAA|title=The Quality of Researchers' Searches of the ERIC Database}}</ref>

Rudner's most cited research project was an examination of the achievement levels of a large sample of home school students.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://epaa.asu.edu/index.php/epaa/article/view/543|title=Achievement and Demographics of Home School Students: 1998}}</ref> This study received coverage in newspapers.<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|date=May 30, 1999|title=No Shortage of Activities for These Home Schoolers|publisher=The Charlotte Observer|page=536}}</ref> He also appeared on ''[[C-SPAN|CSPAN's]]'' ''[[Washington Journal]]'' and the ''[[The Washington Post|Washington Post]]'' to discuss the report.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1999/03/24/a-home-run-for-home-schooling/41408480-8882-4edb-9d57-983bfdec6b45/|title=A Home Run for Home Schooling}}</ref>

In the publication ''What Teachers Need to Know About Assessment'', part of [[National Education Association|NEA's]] Student Assessment Series, Rudner alongside William D. Schafer, provided comprehensive information on [[high-stakes testing]], [[Test score|test scoring]], and [[classroom management]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://beboldnm.pbworks.com/f/assess_principles.pdf|title=What Teachers Need to Know about Assessment}}</ref> He also conducted a report evaluating the IntelliMetric automated essay scoring system's performance compared to human raters using essays from the GMAT Analytic Writing Assessment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ejournals.bc.edu/index.php/jtla/article/view/1651|title=An Evaluation of IntelliMetric™ Essay Scoring System}}</ref>

In 2019, Rudner examined the application of measurement decision theory for classifying examinees, evaluating its effectiveness in terms of classification accuracy, [[Sequential analysis|sequential testing procedures]], and the minimum number of items required for accurate classification.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholarworks.umass.edu/pare/vol14/iss1/8/|title=SCORING AND CLASSIFYING EXAMINEES USING MEASUREMENT DECISION THEORY}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
*2004 – Award for Outstanding Dissemination of Educational Measurement Concepts to the Public, [[National Council on Measurement in Education]]<ref name=aqq/>
*2009 – Career Achievement Award, [[Association of Test Publishers]]<ref name=zll/>

==Selected articles==
*Rudner, L. M. (1980). Biased Item Detection Techniques. Journal of Educational Statistics, 5(3), 213–33.
*Rudner, L. M. (1999). Achievement and Demographics of Home School Students: 1998. Education Policy Analysis Archives, 7(8), 8-8.
*Rudner, L. M., & Liang, T. (2002). Automated essay scoring using Bayes' theorem. The Journal of Technology, Learning and Assessment, 1(2).
*Rudner, L. M., & Schafer, W. D. (2002). What teachers need to know about assessment. National Education Association, 17–20.
*Rudner, L. M. (2019). Expected classification accuracy. Practical Assessment, Research, and Evaluation, 10(1), 13.
*Rudner, L. M. (2019). Scoring and classifying examinees using measurement decision theory. Practical Assessment, Research, and Evaluation, 14(1), 8.
